title: Unchecked checkboxes show a ghost checkmark after toggling a feature off then back on
summary: A fully reproducible Settings UI rendering defect has an open upstream PR from the reporter that explicitly closes the issue and includes automated and manual validation.

judgment.rationale: Open PR #50626 explicitly closes this issue and implements the reported visual correction in the Settings theme resources. The PR includes a before/after recording, reports all 286 Settings.UI.UnitTests passing, and documents manual verification across checkbox-bearing module pages, so starting a separate dashboard fix would duplicate active upstream work.
evidence: The issue supplies numbered reproduction steps and a recording showing unchecked boxes gain a dark ghost glyph after a parent SettingsGroup is disabled and re-enabled.
The behavior is reported across FancyZones, Always On Top, Color Picker, and other Settings pages using checkboxes inside a SettingsGroup.
PR #50626 changes SettingsXAML/App.xaml and Themes/Colors.xaml to make unchecked check-glyph foreground resources transparent.
The PR reports 286 Settings.UI.UnitTests passing and manual verification of the original transition.
judgment.recommended_action: Follow the existing upstream PR #50626; do not create a competing design or reporter request.

fix_assessment.rationale: Open PR #50626 is a concrete upstream fix attempt for the exact visual defect and is linked as a closing pull request.

issue_context.summary: Unchecked WinUI checkboxes can retain a visible glyph after their containing feature is disabled and re-enabled, and a linked upstream PR already addresses the theme resource state.
known_information: The reporter used PowerToys 0.99.1 on Windows 11 and supplied exact steps plus a recording.
The checkbox values remain unchecked; navigating away and back clears only the visual artifact.
The artifact occurs after a Disabled-to-Enabled transition of the parent SettingsGroup.
Open PR #50626 was created by the issue reporter and is linked through the issue timeline.
The PR targets unchecked check-glyph foreground resources in the Settings XAML theme dictionaries.
inferences: The defect is presentation-state leakage rather than an underlying settings-value mutation.
The linked PR's resource override directly targets the glyph that remains visible in the supplied reproduction.
issue_context.analysis: The public issue is already implementation-owned. Its reproduction is sufficient, and the linked PR covers the exact symptom with a narrow Settings theme change and validation evidence. No additional reporter evidence or parallel design is justified.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the complete issue body, recording link, automated triage comment, labels, assignees, and timeline.
Inspected PR #50626 metadata, closing reference, changed files, commit, test claim, and manual validation steps.
Searched the upstream issue set for the exact ghost-checkmark phrase and found no separate superseding issue.

author: T03N

covering_prs.relationship: Closing PR implementing and validating the reported checkbox glyph fix.

upstream_safety.detail: No comments, labels, assignments, closures, or other public mutations were made to microsoft/PowerToys.
